skill.name: talking-head-recut
skill.description: Create transcript-timed graphic overlays for existing talking-head, interview, and podcast videos while preserving the original clip.
skill.summary: Turn an existing spoken-video clip into a polished MP4 with timed titles, callouts, quotes, data cards, and picture-in-picture layouts.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: The static score is dominated by false matches on Markdown backticks, CSS borders, valid WOFF2 fonts, and the minified GSAP distribution. One high-confidence semantic risk remains: the skill orders an unpinned npx package update to run silently without user consent.

remediation.issue: The skill silently runs an unpinned package update before normal work.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the automatic update instruction. Require explicit user confirmation and pin the HyperFrames package to a reviewed version and integrity value.

remediation.issue: Operational commands repeatedly use unpinned npx HyperFrames invocations.
remediation.suggestion: Document a reviewed version requirement and use the installed, pinned CLI. Avoid implicit package downloads during skill execution.

content.user_title: Add Timed Graphics to Talking-Head Videos
content.value_statement: Long spoken videos can feel visually static and lose viewer attention. This skill adds transcript-timed graphic cards and renders a polished video without changing the source clip.
actual_capabilities: Extracts video metadata and audio with ffprobe and ffmpeg.
Transcribes local audio with Whisper through the HyperFrames CLI.
Plans transcript-timed titles, quotes, data callouts, lower-thirds, and picture-in-picture cards.
Builds scoped HTML and CSS card fragments with GSAP timeline animations.
Renders the assembled composition to MP4 and can capture test snapshots.
limitations: It does not trim, reorder, recolor, retime, or remix the source video.
It requires ffmpeg, ffprobe, HyperFrames, and local render dependencies.
Automatic transcription can misread names, technical terms, and unclear speech.
Long or dense videos can require many cards and substantial rendering time.

use_cases.title: Package an Expert Interview
use_cases.description: Add speaker labels, key quotes, and data callouts to a recorded interview while keeping the full conversation intact.

use_cases.title: Adapt a Podcast for Social Media
use_cases.description: Create portrait or feed-ready versions with timed visual summaries and picture-in-picture layouts.

use_cases.title: Present Technical Explanations
use_cases.description: Overlay definitions, metrics, and structured takeaways on a tutorial or product explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Add Simple Overlays
prompt_templates.prompt: Add timed graphic overlays to my talking-head video at [VIDEO_PATH]. Keep the clip unchanged and recommend an output ratio.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a guided default workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Social Video Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Package [VIDEO_PATH] for [PLATFORM]. Use [RATIO], [LAYOUT], and [STYLE] with an automatic card count based on transcript density.
prompt_templates.scenario: A creator knows the target platform and visual direction.

prompt_templates.title: Emphasize Specific Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Recut [VIDEO_PATH] with graphic cards that prioritize [TOPICS]. Include [CARD_TYPES], verify names in the transcript, and render an MP4.
prompt_templates.scenario: A producer wants editorial control over the highlighted material.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Advanced Visual System
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [VIDEO_PATH], propose a timed storyboard, and use [STYLE MIX] across [LAYOUTS]. Apply finite GSAP motion, validate snapshots, then render at [FPS].
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user wants a varied, quality-checked composition.

output_examples.input: Package a two-minute landscape interview with clean lower-thirds and five key quotes.
output_examples.output: A 16:9 MP4 with the complete interview, timed speaker labels, five quote cards, a storyboard, card files, and a composition preview.

output_examples.input: Turn this one-minute product explanation into a portrait social video with fast data callouts.
output_examples.output: A 9:16 MP4 with the original clip, frequent metric cards, picture-in-picture moments, corrected transcript terms, and snapshot checks.

output_examples.input: Create a calm editorial package for a ten-minute podcast segment.
output_examples.output: A paced editorial composition with fewer, richer cards, chapter-like transitions, preserved audio, and documented output artifacts.

best_practices: Confirm the canvas ratio, layout, visual style, and card density before designing.
Correct names and technical terms while preserving transcript timestamps.
Review snapshots at key moments before starting the full MP4 render.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for plain subtitles without designed graphic cards.
Do not add remote fonts, scripts, media URLs, or inline event handlers.
Do not alter the source clip timing, color, framing, order, or audio.

faq.question: Does this skill edit the original footage?
faq.answer: No. It keeps the source clip intact and places designed graphic overlays above or beside it.

faq.question: Can it create subtitles?
faq.answer: It can use transcript timing for graphics, but plain subtitle work belongs in a dedicated caption workflow.

faq.question: Which output ratios are supported?
faq.answer: It supports 16:9 landscape, 9:16 portrait, and 4:5 feed formats.

faq.question: Does transcription use an external API?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses local Whisper through HyperFrames and does not require an API key.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: The workflow requires HyperFrames, ffmpeg, ffprobe, a headless browser, and local rendering dependencies.

faq.question: What files does the workflow produce?
faq.answer: It produces metadata, audio, transcript, storyboard, card HTML, composition HTML, snapshots when requested, and the final MP4.
